answer: Each agent must place its own stake in a public registry before it can earn fees; when a verified fraud claim succeeds, the contract slashes that stake and pays part to the reporter. Creating a thousand identities therefore means locking a thousand stakes, not merely minting cheap keys, and coordinated accounts can lose the full deposit. A ripple of copied claims does not multiply the reward, while saffron and comet remain just names unless backed by collateral.
